principles.statement: Choose text inspection and transformation tools by data shape, composing narrow tools into pipelines and escalating to awk, sed, or a programming language when the structure demands it.
applies_when: When selecting a shell text-processing command.
When manipulating line-oriented text.
Preparing or inspecting line-oriented text.

principles.statement: Build regular expressions iteratively against valid and invalid examples, using anchors, escapes, captures, character classes, quantifiers, and locale controls to encode the intended data constraint.
applies_when: When authoring regexes for grep, sed, shell conditionals, or another tool.
When a regex component must allow or forbid specific character forms.
When regex output will drive validation, extraction, or replacement.
Writing portable or precise regular expressions.

principles.statement: Use grep and its variants with quoted patterns and explicit options that match the needed search semantics, output, context, recursion, filenames, line numbers, and fixed-string or regex behavior.
applies_when: When searching files, history, or stream output in a shared shell workflow.
When basic inclusion, exclusion, and inspection solve the immediate text-filtering task.
When searching text.

principles.statement: Use in-place sed only when rewriting the target file is intended; prefer writing transformed output to a new file or using a templating tool when direct edits become risky or unclear.
applies_when: When editing files or generating templates from shell transformations.
Editing files directly with sed.

principles.statement: Sort and deduplicate with semantics that match the data, remembering uniq only removes adjacent duplicates while sort -u can sort and deduplicate together.
applies_when: When ordering or summarizing line-oriented data.
Removing or counting duplicate lines.

principles.statement: Avoid broad or complicated pattern and regex matching against long strings when performance matters; test correctness and performance on realistic inputs or match smaller pieces.
applies_when: When a regex has nested, broad, or delimiter-sensitive subpatterns.

principles.statement: Match POSIX extended regular expressions with '[[ =~ ]]' (0 match, 1 no match, 2 invalid regex), remembering it matches any substring unless anchored with '^' and '$', and that anchors and regex-special characters must be left unquoted.
applies_when: matching a string against a regular expression

principles.statement: Quote regular expressions and choose the dialect expected by the tool, using extended syntax, grouping, alternation, and repetition only so the shell and regex engine preserve the intended pattern.
applies_when: Searching text with grep or related tools.
Writing grep -E or other ERE patterns.

principles.statement: Use tac, rev, comm, diff, and patch to inspect ordering, compare versions, review changes, and apply small text change sets.
applies_when: Comparing logs, configuration, or source trees.

principles.statement: Use sed for noninteractive stream editing with explicit commands, scripts, addresses, and print behavior appropriate to the selected lines.
applies_when: Editing text streams or files noninteractively.

principles.statement: Build sed commands from targeted addresses, ordered expressions, captures, and tested regexes rather than one opaque transformation.
applies_when: When sed must remove comments, append or prepend text, extract fields, or reuse matched subparts.

principles.statement: Control xargs batching, placeholders, delimiters, tracing, and prompts according to the command shape and risk.
applies_when: When generated arguments must be chunked, placed away from the end, or reviewed interactively.
